title: Orchard Fields Scheme Report - Q2 2026/27
author: P034
summary: Quarterly report on the three-phase Orchard Fields regeneration: phase 1 handover and lettings, phase 2 construction progress and delay, phase 3 planning and the board decision due February 2027.

blocks.p: Orchard Fields is a three-phase mixed-tenure scheme of {{sql:SELECT SUM(homes) FROM developments WHERE scheme LIKE 'Orchard Fields%'|int}} homes on the former Shepway allotment and garage site in Maidstone ME15, plus a community hub and two shops in phase 3. All three phases are built by Castlemere Construction Ltd under a design and build contract. It is the largest scheme in our history and the centrepiece of the 'Home First' corporate plan.

table.sql: SELECT scheme AS Phase, homes AS Homes, tenure_mix AS "Tenure mix", status AS Status, start_on_site AS "Start on site", completion AS Completion, total_scheme_cost_gbp AS "Scheme cost", homes_england_grant_gbp AS "HE grant", notes AS Notes FROM developments WHERE scheme LIKE 'Orchard Fields%' ORDER BY dev_id
table.caption: Table 1 - Orchard Fields phases (from the development pipeline)

blocks.p: Practical completion of phase 1 was certified on 2 October 2026, nine weeks later than the contract date of 31 July 2026. Castlemere's extension of time claim (weather and the UK Power Networks substation connection) was accepted for five weeks; liquidated damages of £38,400 have been deducted for the remaining four weeks.

Lettings began on 6 October. {{sql:SELECT COUNT(*) FROM properties WHERE scheme_id='SCH14' AND status='Occupied'|int}} homes are occupied and {{fact:newbuild_awaiting_let}} are awaiting their first let, mostly shared ownership homes waiting for buyers' mortgage offers and affordable rent homes held back while defects are fixed.

Residents have reported {{sql:SELECT COUNT(*) FROM repairs WHERE scheme_id='SCH14'|int}} repairs in the first month. Most are new-build defects that are Castlemere's responsibility in the 12-month defects liability period. Raising them as repairs in FieldLoop is causing confusion about who pays (see the handover report and the defects log).

Phase 2 started on site on 3 November 2025. The programme is two months behind after the groundworks delay (an uncharted culvert and additional piling). Castlemere's revised programme shows completion on 30 September 2027. The phase 2 appraisal (v3, September 2025) has not yet been updated for the revised dates or the extra piling cost of £186,000.

blocks.h1: 4. Phase 3 and community hub - planning approved

blocks.p: Planning consent for 44 homes, the community hub and two retail units was granted in June 2026. The tenure mix is to be confirmed. The Board will decide in February 2027 whether to proceed, depending on the business plan refresh and the interest cover forecast.

title: Shared Ownership - Frequently Asked Questions and Staircasing Guide
author: P035
summary: Plain-English answers for buyers and shared owners: how shared ownership works, rent and service charges, repairs, staircasing (including 1% staircasing on new model leases), resales and subletting.

blocks.p: You buy a share of your home (usually between 10% and 75%) with a mortgage or savings, and pay a subsidised rent to Silvering Homes on the share you don't own. You can buy more shares later - this is called staircasing. We currently have {{sql:SELECT COUNT(*) FROM properties WHERE tenure='Shared ownership'|int}} shared ownership homes.

Households with an income of £80,000 or less who cannot afford to buy a suitable home on the open market and do not own another home. Members of the armed forces and local residents or workers get priority at Orchard Fields under the section 106 agreement.

Rent starts at 2.75% a year of the value of the share you don't own. It increases each April in line with your lease: CPI + 1% for leases signed since 2021, or RPI + 0.5% for older leases. In April 2026 the Board capped increases at 4.8%.

blocks.h3: Do I pay a service charge?

blocks.p: Yes. You pay a service charge for shared services (for example grounds maintenance and communal lighting) and buildings insurance, plus a management fee. You pay 100% of the service charge whatever share you own.

As a shared owner you are responsible for all repairs inside your home, as an owner-occupier would be. On **new model leases** (from April 2021, including all Orchard Fields homes) Silvering will cover the cost of essential repairs to the structure and exterior for the first 10 years, up to £500 a year. In the first 12 months of a new home, defects are fixed by the builder - report them to us and we will pass them on.

blocks.h3: How do I buy more shares?

numbered: Tell us in writing (or through MySilvering) that you want to staircase.
We instruct an RICS valuer; you pay the valuation fee (around £350). The valuation is valid for 3 months.
We send you a staircasing offer showing the price of the extra share and your new rent.
Your solicitor completes the purchase. If you reach 100%, you own the home outright (freehold for houses, extended lease for flats).

blocks.h3: Can I staircase in small steps?

blocks.p: Yes, if you have a new model lease you can buy 1% a year for the first 15 years, at a price based on the original value indexed by the House Price Index, with no valuation fee. On older leases the minimum is 10% per transaction.

If you want to sell, you must tell us first. We have an 8-week nomination period (4 weeks on new model leases) to find a buyer through our waiting list before you can sell on the open market. You can only sell your share at current market value as set by an RICS valuation.
You cannot sublet your home unless we agree in writing in exceptional circumstances (for example a temporary job move or armed forces posting).
Sales and shared ownership team: {{person:P035}}, {{person:P035.email}}, {{person:P035.phone}}.

subject: Orchard Fields phase 1 - defects escalation
summary: Paul Whitaker escalates overdue Orchard Fields defects to Castlemere's project director after the remediation plan promised at the 22 October site meeting is not received; Castlemere replies and Tom Lyle proposes withholding further retention.

messages.body:
Neil,

I'm writing formally to escalate the defects position at Orchard Fields phase 1.

At our site meeting on 22 October you agreed to send a full defects remediation plan by 29 October, with dates for every open item and a named supervisor. We have not received it.

Since then:

- Five flats (41-45) still have uncommissioned MVHR, a month after practical completion. One family at flat 44 now has mould in a bedroom. We have to deal with this under Awaab's Law timescales whether or not it's your defect.
- Three flat entrance fire doors are still not compliant.
- 41 defects are past the 28-day target, and you missed the 4-hour emergency attendance three times on heat pumps.
- We still don't have the as-built drawings or the MVHR and heat pump O&M manuals.

Our in-house team has attended several of these to keep residents safe. We will recharge those costs.

Please send the remediation plan by 12 noon on Thursday 5 November, and confirm the MVHR commissioning date for all five flats. If we don't receive it I will recommend that we use the retention to bring in another contractor.

Regards,
Paul

Paul,

Apologies for the delay on the plan. Our aftercare manager has been off sick and I should have picked this up.

The MVHR commissioning engineer is booked for 6 November for all five flats. Door closers arrive on 9 November. I'll send the full programme by Thursday.

On flat 44, our view is that the mould is condensation from drying washing indoors rather than a defect, but we'll inspect with your surveyor.

I don't accept that you can recharge for attendances where we weren't given the chance to attend. Can we discuss on Thursday?

Neil Garside
Project Director, Castlemere Construction Ltd

Paul,

Good email. Two things:

1. Flat 44: please get Ellie to inspect alongside them, not just Castlemere. Without working MVHR, 'lifestyle' is not an answer we'll accept, and the clock is running for us under Awaab's Law.

2. I'd like to hold the second half of the retention (£186,250) until the defects are below 20 and the as-builts are in. Martin - are you OK with that given the V2 pressure?

Also, has anyone told Homes England about phase 2? That action has been on the list since September.

Tom

title: Orchard Fields monthly site progress meeting
summary: Monthly progress meeting with Castlemere: phase 1 defects after handover, MVHR and fire doors, the flat 4 mould case, phase 2 programme and the piling claim.
agenda: Phase 2 programme and piling compensation event

transcript.text: Morning everyone. I think we're just waiting on Martin... oh, there he is. Right, let's start. Neil, health and safety first?
Yeah, morning. Nothing reportable. Aisha's put the fencing check into close-down like we said last month, and no repeat of the near miss.
We did have a delivery driver come in at seven-forty on Monday, which, sorry, we've had words.

Okay, thanks. Brenchley residents did notice, so keep on it. Phase 1 defects. I'll be honest, this is the bit I'm worried about. We're three weeks after handover and we've still got around a hundred and forty open.
It's coming down, Paul. We closed about twenty this week.
And residents raised about fifteen new ones. So it's basically flat. The big ones for me are the MVHR in flats forty-one to forty-five and the fire doors.
The MVHR is with the specialist sub. They've, um, they've got the commissioning engineer, but he's not available until early November.
Early November is a month after people moved in. That was a condition of PC. It's in the minutes from September.
It is. I wrote it on the certificate as well. PC was conditional on MVHR and fire doors before occupation.
Understood. I'll push the sub, but I can't magic up an engineer.

Can I come in on that? I've had a damp and mould report from number four, which is a family with a young child. Mould in the child's bedroom. And flat forty-four is reporting black spots. Without ventilation working, new builds will get condensation, they're drying out.
Ellie, is number four an Awaab's Law case?

Yes. It's significant, there's a child in the household. So we have to investigate within ten working days and get the summary out within three. I've done the inspection. I think there's a missing cavity tray above the window, it's not just condensation.
We'll get our site manager to look at the cavity tray. If it's that, it's ours.
I need a date, though, because I have to tell the resident when the safety works start.
Next Wednesday, the twenty-eighth. I'll put it in writing.

Can I raise the FieldLoop thing? My lads are being sent out to Orchard Fields jobs because residents ring us and it goes straight into FieldLoop. Some of those are clearly defects. Who's paying for those visits?
Those should come to me first. There's no DLP flag in FieldLoop yet. Craig's meant to be adding it.
And for the record, we can't accept recharges where we weren't given the chance to attend.
Except emergencies where you didn't turn up in four hours. Flat one had no heating for seven hours.
Fair, that one's on us.
So what I need, Neil, is a proper remediation plan. Every open defect, a date, and who's doing it. Can you get that to me by next Thursday, the twenty-ninth?
Twenty-ninth. Yes, I'll get that to you.
And the as-builts, please. They're overdue too, and Homes England will want them for the audit.
As-builts by the thirtieth.
Okay. Phase 2. Martin, where are you on the piling claim?

I think it's a valid compensation event. The culvert wasn't on the site investigation. I'd value it lower than a hundred and eighty-six, nearer a hundred and sixty, but I'll put that in writing next week.
Either way it's not in the appraisal. I'll need to rerun the phase 2 numbers. And completion's now end of September next year, isn't it?
Thirtieth of September. We might claw a couple of weeks back on the frame, but I wouldn't promise it.
Right. Has the revised programme gone to Homes England? I think that was mine. ... No, it hasn't, has it. I'll do that.
Please do. They don't like surprises on PC milestones.
Resident liaison: Steve, anything?
Just that the bin store lock on block B is broken and someone's dumped a mattress. Not a big one but residents are noticing.
I'll get that fixed this week.
Great. Anything else? ... No? Okay, thanks all. Next one's the nineteenth of November.

recap.summary: Phase 1 defects remain at around 140 open three weeks after handover. MVHR in five flats and three fire doors are still outstanding despite being conditions of practical completion. A significant damp and mould case at 4 Orchard Fields is being handled under Awaab's Law. Castlemere agreed to send a full remediation plan by 29 October and as-built drawings by 30 October. Phase 2 completion is now 30 September 2027 and the piling compensation event is being assessed.
